meta.tagline: Capital of Europe, homeland of Christmas, one city of two cultures

pills: The cathedral is 142 m — once the world's tallest

overview.title: Welcome to Strasbourg
overview.intro: Strasbourg stands squarely between two worlds and absorbs them both: you buy a croissant from a French bakery in the morning and eat choucroute with a German appetite at noon. Everyone who sees the Gothic cathedral stops for a moment; the canal houses of Petite France, meanwhile, have arrived to meet your fairytale expectations. Add the glass palaces of the European Parliament and you get a city hard to describe and easy to explore.

local_word.definition: Alsatian for 'room, parlour': the root of winstub (wine parlour). Wood panelling, a tiled stove and strangers sharing your table — the stub is the architectural unit of Strasbourg's warmth.

rules.title: Don't miss the cathedral's clock
rules.description: The astronomical clock's apostles parade daily at 12:30; be inside by noon for the short show. The tower's 332 steps spread the Alsatian plain out to the Black Forest — climb in the morning while the queue is short.

rules.title: Think of the city by bicycle
rules.description: Strasbourg is France's most bike-friendly city: 600 km of paths, dead-flat ground, Vélhop rentals on every corner. With two wheels, the European Quarter and the Orangerie are pedalling — not walking — distance.

rules.title: December is planned separately
rules.description: The Christkindelsmärik, held since 1570, is France's oldest Christmas market; in December the city transforms. Book hotel and train months ahead for that season.

quick_facts.label: Language
quick_facts.sub: German widespread, Alsatian alive on the street

tip.label: The Strasbourg philosophy
tip.text: This city has lived both sides of the border and forgiven both; its identity is not 'either-or' but 'both-and'. Don't choose either: bretzel at noon, croissant at dusk — that's the Strasbourg way.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: The central island walks, the rest is woven by tram; the bicycle is the city's mother tongue.

items.title: Arrival — by TGV
items.description: 1 hour 46 minutes from Paris; the station is a 10-minute walk from the Grande Île. Colmar 30, Basel 80 minutes — the natural base camp for an Alsace trip.

items.title: The tram network
items.description: Six modern lines weave the city and suburbs; line D crosses the Rhine into the German town of Kehl — changing countries by tram is a pleasure peculiar to Strasbourg.

items.title: Vélhop bikes
items.description: In France's cycling capital the rental network is dense and cheap; the canal-side routes and the European Quarter are loveliest by pedal.

items.title: The Grande Île on foot
items.description: The UNESCO-listed central island is 25 minutes end to end: cathedral, Petite France and the quays fit into a single walk.

items.title: The Batorama boat tour
items.description: The classic 70-minute loop from the canals to the European Parliament; seeing the city from the water is worth it, especially in evening light.

callout.label: Kehl tip
callout.text: Cross into Germany in 20 minutes on tram D, shop the Kehl market, and walk the footbridge joining the two countries at the Jardin des Deux Rives. No one asks for a passport, and you keep the story.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Strasbourg the question is: do you want to sleep inside the fairytale, or a stroll away from it?

local_word.definition: The famous carved timber house of 1427 on the cathedral square: the spiritual emblem of Strasbourg lodging. Even if you don't sleep inside, raise your head every time you pass.

items.name: Grande Île — around the cathedral
items.description: The heart of the UNESCO island: wake in the cathedral's shadow and walk everywhere. Busy around the square by day, but at night the city is yours; in December the magic here doubles.

items.name: Petite France — canal houses
items.description: The old tanners' quarter where half-timbered houses lean over the water: morning mist, swans, façades that fill camera rolls. Rooms are few and demand high — book early.

items.name: Krutenau — student soul
items.description: The young, cheerful quarter just southeast of the centre: small bars, world kitchens, fair prices. Perfect for nightlife seekers and long stays.

items.name: Around the station — practical base
items.description: Around the glass-domed historic station: chain hotels, easy luggage logistics, 10 minutes' walk to the centre. Sensible for those touring Alsace by train.

items.name: Neustadt — the imperial quarter
items.description: The German-era 'new town' of broad boulevards and art nouveau façades: calm, green, and the lesser-known second half of the UNESCO listing. For those after elegance away from the crowds.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Strasbourg's calendar splits in two: December, and the other eleven months. Both have their case.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Canal Season
items.subtitle: Spring · Flowering quays, cycling weather
items.description: Petite France blooms, terraces go up, cycling season opens. Crowds stay below summer levels and the light is a photographer's friend — the city's most balanced stretch.

callout.label: June tip
callout.text: On June evenings a light show is projected onto the cathedral façade; spread a blanket on the square — the show is free.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Terrace Season
items.subtitle: Summer · Long evenings, river cool
items.description: The days stretch, the quay terraces overflow, the boat tours add night sailings. On hot days the canal banks and parks are the city's air conditioning.

callout.label: Summer tip
callout.text: When the heat presses, escape to the Orangerie: shade beneath the stork nests, ice cream by the lake.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Vines and Mist
items.subtitle: Autumn · Harvest nearby, misty mornings
items.description: The Wine Route's harvest is half an hour away; in town, misty mornings turn Petite France into a film set. By late November the Christmas preparations begin and the lights go up.

callout.label: October tip
callout.text: In October day-trip to Obernai or Barr: harvest festivals, new wine and onion tart — Alsace without the tourists.

items.label: Winter
items.name: The Capital of Christmas
items.subtitle: Winter · Christkindelsmärik, light and cinnamon
items.description: In December the city earns its title: over 300 chalets, a giant tree, the smell of cinnamon and mulled wine, and a tradition running since 1570. January and February leave behind a silent, misty, authentic Strasbourg.

callout.label: December warning
callout.text: Christmas market weekends are intensely crowded; come midweek — live the market by evening light and the streets in morning silence.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The Strasbourg table is Alsatian cooking in its capital form: portions German, finesse French, appetite yours.

local_word.definition: Alsatian for 'cheers': said when the glasses fill with Riesling. Santé works too, but the moment you say s'gilt your place at the table changes — promoted from guest to friend.

items.name: Tarte flambée — thin and from the embers
items.description: The thin dough with cream, onion and bacon is Alsace's pride; in Strasbourg the 'gratinée' (with cheese) and the sweet apple version also make the table. Broken by hand, gone in a minute.
items.tag: In a winstub · order in rounds

items.name: Choucroute and baeckeoffe
items.description: The monumental fermented-cabbage plate reigns here too; baeckeoffe, the three-meat casserole slow-baked overnight in wine, is the secret hero of winter days.

items.name: Bretzel — warm
items.description: A warm bretzel from a street bakery is the official snack of the Strasbourg stroll; the buttered and cheese-topped ones are an invitation to sin.
items.tag: Warm from the oven · while walking

items.name: Foie gras d'Alsace
items.description: Foie gras has centuries of history in Alsace; served with brioche and a sweet white (Gewurztraminer), it opens a feast.

items.name: Alsace glasses — Riesling to Crémant
items.description: You are at the gate of the Wine Route: from the winstub jug to a flute of Crémant, the whole range lives here. When the long green-stemmed Alsace glass reaches your hand, the ritual is complete.

items.name: Bredele and pain d'épices
items.description: Bredele, the Christmas cookie army, fills every December window; spiced honey bread pain d'épices is the city's scent all year round. Buy a tin — it won't last.

callout.label: The winstub rule
callout.text: In tourist hours, step one or two streets off the cathedral square: the real winstubs wait in Krutenau and the back lanes of Petite France, with short menus and a noise of Alsatian.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Gems
hidden_gems.intro: The cathedral calls everyone; these six corners call only the curious.

items.name: The Barrage Vauban terrace
items.description: The roof terrace of the 17th-century dam-bridge looks over the covered towers of Petite France to the cathedral: the city's best panorama, free entry, and most visitors never hear of it.

items.name: The apartments of Palais Rohan
items.description: The bishops' palace at the cathedral's foot hides three museums at once; the rococo apartments downstairs offer the air of Versailles without the queues.

items.name: The Orangerie's stork nests
items.description: Storks, Alsace's emblem bird, have built a colony in the treetops of the Orangerie; in spring their bill-clattering is the park's background music.

items.name: The BNU reading room
items.description: The domed reading room of the National University Library in Neustadt is the city's calmest masterpiece; you may enter and breathe even without a student card.

items.name: The towers of the Ponts Couverts
items.description: The 'covered bridges' — named for wooden roofs long gone — and their medieval towers give the city's least-known postcard when the evening lights come on.

items.rarity: The glass ship of the modern
items.name: The European Parliament bank
items.description: Walk or pedal the canal bank to the glass parliament: visits are possible in session periods, the architecture is open from outside always. The idea of Europe in concrete and glass.

callout.label: Panorama tip
callout.text: For those who skip the cathedral tower, the formula is: Barrage Vauban terrace + evening light. Ninety percent of the view, zero percent of the steps.

traps.title: Skip the Traps
traps.intro: Strasbourg is a fair-minded city; its traps are squeezed into a hundred metres around the cathedral square. Know these four and you're done.

items.name: The 'Alsatian menu' right on the cathedral square
items.description: Some square-view terraces sell frozen choucroute at tourist prices; an injustice to Alsatian cooking.
items.instead: Walk two streets: in the winstubs of Krutenau and the back lanes the same dish arrives at half the price, in its true form.

items.name: Mass-produced 'handmade' at the Christmas market
items.description: Among 300 chalets, imported ornaments and factory goods slip in; same sparkle, no story.
items.instead: Pick the producers' chalets: you'll know the Alsace pottery, wood carving and local bredele sellers by their labels and their conversation.

items.name: The midday boat queue
items.description: Batorama queues run long at noon, and 70 minutes in a covered boat under the midday sun is the tour at its dullest.
items.instead: Book the first morning or early-evening sailing online: beautiful light, no queue.

items.name: A cold bretzel on the square
items.description: A rubbery bretzel waiting on a tourist stand is the most unnecessary crime this city can witness.
items.instead: Take it warm from a bakery; you can't go wrong where the window says 'artisan boulanger'.

callout.label: The golden rule
callout.text: In Strasbourg the crowd thins in rings out from the cathedral: every hundred metres of distance lowers the price and raises the sincerity. Walk two rings out.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: Cathedral, canals and a winstub evening

steps.title: The cathedral — in morning light
steps.description: See the rose window with the morning sun; if your legs allow, climb the 332 steps to the platform — the Alsatian plain at your feet.

steps.title: The lanes of Petite France
steps.description: Half-timbered houses along the canal, tanners' roofs, swans; drift between the photo stops.

steps.title: Astronomical clock + lunch
steps.description: Watch the apostles parade at 12:30, then a round of tarte flambée at a back-street winstub.

steps.title: Barrage Vauban + Ponts Couverts
steps.description: From the terrace panorama to the towers, then a quay walk; the city's defensive history reads on the water.

steps.title: Boat or tram to the European Quarter
steps.description: By Batorama or by bike along the bank of glass institutions; a stork stop in the Orangerie on the way back.

steps.title: Winstub evening
steps.description: Baeckeoffe or choucroute, Riesling in the green-stemmed glass; close with s'gilt!

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Live the city as a guest, not a tourist

steps.title: Grande Île classics
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: cathedral, Petite France, Vauban, winstub.

steps.title: Neustadt and two countries
steps.description: Imperial boulevards and the BNU dome in the morning, Palais Rohan at noon; cross to Kehl on tram D in the afternoon, walk the footbridge between two countries, finish in the bars of Krutenau.

steps.title: A Wine Route escape
steps.description: By train to Obernai or Colmar: wine villages, tastings and a winstub lunch; back to Strasbourg at night for a farewell lap of the cathedral in its evening lights.

phrases.title: The 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: French opens the doors; a pinch of Alsatian changes your seat at the table.

items.meaning: Hello — the mandatory first word of every exchange
Please — add it to the end of your order
Alsatian cheers! — Riesling glasses rise to this
The Alsatian joker word: 'come on, okay, there' — you'll hear it ten times a day

items.label: Stand under the cathedral's rose window
items.sub: In morning light, until your neck aches

items.label: Watch the apostles of the astronomical clock
items.sub: Daily at 12:30 — enter early, claim a spot

items.label: Walk Petite France in the morning mist
items.sub: The canal houses at their finest

items.label: Climb to the Barrage Vauban terrace
Do a tarte flambée round in a winstub
Drink Riesling from the green-stemmed glass
Take the tram to Germany
items.sub: Line D — 20 minutes to Kehl, no passport

items.label: Find a stork nest in the Orangerie
items.sub: Alsace's emblem bird in the treetops

items.label: Leave with a tin of bredele
items.sub: From the market in December, from a bakery otherwise
